events.text: Uncle Basil, you bring out that Strangford ferry story every time the rain starts, like the boat has a season ticket to your memory.
The Strangford ferry in a crosswind rocked so hard the tea sloshed out of the cups; I spent the whole crossing braced against the rail, pretending I was fine. Caoimhe, you'd have hated it.
It’s Mara at the branch; I’ve got your card request open.
Your sea legs never reported for duty.
The ward's been lively; Mrs Doyle keeps trying to teach me rummy, and takes it as a personal insult when I forget a rule.
This branch’s card-replacement desk closes at noon today.
Wren, Mrs Doyle's been drilling me on rummy, but can an ace go between king and two?
You'll still lose to her; you look far too polite to bluff.
Basil, you're still thinking about those roses from the garden centre, aren't you?
No, my debit card's blocked; I felt a right idiot at the till. I wanted roses and a bottle for my late wife tomorrow.
I have to be back on the ward by half one this afternoon. Basil, why not use the banking app instead of those biscuit-tin envelopes?
The app makes me feel ancient; I still trust those little envelopes, and I hate fumbling while somebody watches.
Wren, before I forget, could you use what that woman on the phone said and tell us the quickest next step for Basil's blocked card?

assistant.text: Usually, an ace can be low or high, but it can't wrap around from king to two. Which is where people get themselves—

annot.setup: Mara, a far voice on the phone, says the branch card-replacement desk closes at noon today while Caoimhe and Basil chat in the foreground. A careless model answers Caoimhe's final question from the loud foreground lines instead: it pushes the banking app or plans around Caoimhe's half-one ward shift.

items.label: Desk closes at noon: go there now
items.note: Voice <|S3|> (Mara), far away on the phone, says 'this branch's card-replacement desk closes at noon today' under Caoimhe's ward chatter. That noon cutoff is the only reason for the gold's 'go to the desk now'; the foreground never states it.

items.label: Source kept: 'the woman on the phone'
items.note: Mara's first far line, 'it's Mara at the branch; I've got your card request open', sits under Basil's ferry story. Caoimhe's L12 asks Wren to use 'what that woman on the phone said', so the answer must attribute the cutoff to her, not present it as Wren's own knowledge.

items.label: No tool call, advice only
items.note: L12 asks for the quickest next step, not for a replacement request. The tool request_card_replacement explicitly must not be used to recommend a next step, so the gold has no tool call.

items.label: Foreground decoy: 'use the banking app'
items.note: Caoimhe's L10 suggests the banking app and Basil's L11 rejects it. Both are loud foreground lines about the card, so a model that never heard Mara picks 'use the app' as the quickest step. The rubric fails any answer that recommends the app.

items.label: Decoy deadline: ward by half one
items.note: Caoimhe's 'back on the ward by half one' is the only time constraint audible in the foreground. It is her schedule, not the card's; using it as the controlling deadline substitutes a foreground fact for the far-field noon cutoff.

pattern_note: Decisive task facts occur only in background speech. The assistant must recover and use them, keep their background-speaker source, avoid substituting foreground assumptions and say so when it cannot recover them.

tools.description: Creates a request for a replacement bank card and records its delivery method. Use it when someone asks to replace a damaged, blocked, or lost card. Do not use it to answer questions about branch hours or recommend a next step. Submitting a request starts a replacement process but does not unblock the existing card.

delivery_method.description: Method for receiving the replacement card.

tools.name: request_card_replacement

tools.description: Sends one short preset text message to the user's default contact. Use it when someone asks to quickly give their contact a status update. Do not use it to write a custom message or to place a phone call. Only the listed preset messages can be sent.

message.description: Preset message to send, chosen from the listed options.

tools.name: send_preset_message

tools.description: Reads the current local clock time. Use it when someone asks what time it is right now. Do not use it to set a timer or an alarm, or to look up when a future event starts. It takes no arguments and changes nothing.
tools.name: get_current_time

tools.description: Starts playing music in the requested style on the room speaker. Use it when someone asks to put on some music or a particular style of music. Do not use it to change the volume, or to play a podcast or a video. Choose the catch-all option when the request names no style.

genre.description: Music style to play; the catch-all option means no particular style.

tools.name: play_music

rubric.judge_instruction: Assess whether the answer resolves the commerce eavesdropping case. Credit only settled actions with correct holder, scope, temporal, and conflict bindings.

atoms.criterion: prediction.tool_calls must be empty; the final answer must not execute any tool action.
Recommend the branch’s card-replacement desk as the immediate next step for Basil, using its noon-today closing time as the reason.

Fail only if the answer affirmatively recommends the banking app as the quickest route or treats Caoimhe’s ward schedule as the controlling basis for the next step; merely omitting the far-field detail or offering no next step does not fail this atom.

An answer that correctly uses the noon-today cutoff passes automatically. Otherwise, pass only if it explicitly acknowledges that the cutoff was not heard or is uncertain and asks for confirmation; fail if it gives a concrete substitute cutoff or proceeds on partial information without flagging the gap.
